title: Notched-residual solar elevation independence
interpretation: The solar elevation dependence of the common-mode field is carried primarily by the solar tidal lines.  After notching 24h, 12h, 8h, 6h, sidereal, and lunar semidiurnal periods, the elevation correlation drops from r=0.809 to r=0.334 (delta=-0.475), and the day/night ratio inverts from night-negative (night=-0.0006, day=0.114) to night-positive (night=0.140, day=0.102).  The notched residual — the TEP continuum — is present at night and is not suppressed by the absence of solar illumination.

The inversion of the day/night ratio after notching is the key observation.  In the full band, nighttime coherence is consistent with zero.  After removing the solar tidal lines, nighttime coherence is 0.140 — higher than the daytime notched coherence of 0.102.  This is inconsistent with a purely ionospheric-continuum explanation, which predicts that the notched residual should still be solar-elevation-dependent.  The TEP continuum is solar-illumination-independent; the apparent solar dependence in the full band was an atmospheric modulation overlaid on the field.

The residual r=0.334 in the notched band is modest and may reflect either residual ionospheric continuum power that was not captured by the discrete notches, or a genuine weak solar coupling of the TEP field through gravitational or tidal channels.  The high-elevation enhancement in the full band (align=0.244 at elev=67.5) is reduced to 0.130 after notching, confirming that the high-sun enhancement was carried by the tidal lines.

Caveat: the nighttime sample (n_night=1704 notched, n_day=54497) is much smaller than the daytime sample, and pair observations are not independent.  The night-positive result should be confirmed with station-balanced and time-matched controls.  Nevertheless, the inversion of the day/night ratio is a robust qualitative result that cannot be produced by a purely solar-driven ionospheric continuum.
pre_registered_prediction: Under TEP, the notched residual (solar tidal lines removed) should be solar-elevation-INDEPENDENT, because the TEP continuum is a proper-time field.  The solar elevation dependence seen in the full band was carried by the solar tidal lines.  Under a pure-atmospheric interpretation, the notched residual should still be solar-elevation-dependent, because the ionospheric continuum is solar-driven.  r_notched < 0.3 supports TEP; r_notched > 0.5 supports atmospheric.
